mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over the preceding three months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by >0.25% per month for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (<-1.5% mean) in periods where this trigger is met, or the trigger fires but returns are positive in >60% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (<-1.0% mean) when this trigger is met, or the trigger is met but returns are positive in >50% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 6% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (<-1.0% mean) when UNRATE exceeds 6% for two months, or the trigger is met but returns are positive in >50% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) for three consecutive months indicates weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces earnings for industrial firms and drags down S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (<-1.0% mean) when INDPRO declines for three months, or the trigger is met but returns are positive in >50% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both the housing starts index (HOUST) and personal savings rate (RSAFS) signals a shift from saving to investment, which boosts future consumption and capital expenditure, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and RSAFS both rise month-over-month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (>0.5% mean) when both HOUST and RSAFS rise month-over-month, or the joint trigger is met but returns are negative in >60% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in both CPIAUCSL and FEDFUNDS above their respective 12-month averages signals an inflationary shock met with a policy response, which increases uncertainty and volatility, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL > 12-mo avg AND FEDFUNDS > 12-mo avg in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative (<-1.0% mean) when both CPIAUCSL and FEDFUNDS exceed their 12-month averages, or the joint trigger is met but returns are positive in >60% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid acceleration in payroll employment growth (PAYEMS) above 250k per month for two consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which boosts consumer spending and corporate profits, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days, except during periods of high inflation.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (>1.0% mean) when PAYEMS exceeds 250k for two months in a low inflation regime, or the trigger is met but returns are negative in >50% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: An always-on positive correlation exists between real personal consumption expenditures growth (proxied by GDPC1 YoY change) and S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days, regardless of regime, due to forward-looking earnings revisions by market participants.
failure_condition: No significant positive correlation (p > 0.10) between GDPC1 YoY growth and S&P 500 60-day forward returns in out-of-sample walk-forward tests.
